Scale an rwl object for TSAP export

Source: R/extract_rwl.R
scale_for_tsap.Rd

write_tsap() writes values rounded to integers, as TSAP expects ring widths in μm (typically 300–2000). QWA parameters on smaller scales (e.g. cell wall thickness, or relative measures well below 1) would lose most or all of their information. This function scales an rwl object (as returned by extract_rwl()) by a power-of-ten factor. By default, the factor is chosen automatically as the largest that keeps all values at most 9999 (4 integer digits).

Usage

scale_for_tsap(rwl, scaling = NULL)

Arguments

rwl

A dplR rwl object, e.g. as returned by extract_rwl().

scaling

Numeric power of ten to scale by, or NULL (default) to determine the factor automatically.

Value

The scaled rwl object, with the applied factor as attribute "scaling".

Details

Ring-width parameters in μm (e.g. mrw, eww, lww) need no scaling. Auto-scaling would instead scale series with all values below 1000 by 10 or more.

A manual scaling must be a power of ten and keep all values within the integer range (at most .Machine$integer.max). The applied factor is stored in the "scaling" attribute of the returned rwl object; dividing the exported values by scaling gives back the original values (up to rounding). An rwl object that already has a "scaling" attribute is not scaled again. The attribute is dropped by most other operations (e.g. subsetting, arithmetic, dplR functions), so apply this function as the last step before writing.

See also

scale_for_tucson() for Tucson-format writing.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
rwl <- extract_rwl(df_rings = QWA_data$rings, param = "cwtrad_mean",
                   prf_data = prf_sector, sector = 5)
scaled <- scale_for_tsap(rwl)
attr(scaled, "scaling")
write_tsap(scaled, "cwtrad_mean_tsap.txt")
} # }
